earlier_scan.note: Extinct, poorly attested Arawakan; only wordlists (Tessmann 1930, Fleck 2007); no phonological description exists.

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2022. Homonimia de etnónimos en la familia Pano. Amazonía Peruana 35: 64-88. Lima: CAAAP. DOI 10.52980/revistaamazonaperuana.vi35.300.
sources.note: Nothing. Full text searched for acento/acentuación/tónica/prosodia/tono/fonología: no hits except one 'fonología' about Capistrano de Abreu's 1914 Kashinawa monograph. Moríke/Mayú are mentioned only to exclude Tessmann's 'Mayoruna' from the Panoan family (identity and lexical-percentage remarks, the text layerTabla 1 line 85 ff., appendix row line 440).

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History 99.
sources.note: Nothing on Morike stress. Moríke appears only in passing: p. 20 note g ('Also known as Moríke; see Fleck (2007d) for discussion of Mayoruna homonymy'), p. 30 note 20 ('the Arawakan-like Moríke or Mayú'), and the bibliography entry for Fleck 2007d (p. 57).

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2007. ¿Quiénes eran los Mayoruna (Moríke) de Tessmann? Amazonía Peruana 30: 305-331.
sources.note: The only modern study: identifies Tessmann's 'Mayoruna' as Moríke, adds the Mayú wordlist (Cuibusio, SIL 1975) and compares both with Chamicuro; likely re-transcribes Tessmann's forms and may comment on accent marks. Comparative wordlist paper, not a phonology.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record for Morike [mori1273], with reference records 31931 (Fleck 2007) and 34227 (Tessmann 1930)
sources.note: Nothing. Only two descriptive refs, both typed a wordlist or less (Fleck 2007, comparative;wordlist; Tessmann 1930, overview;comparative;wordlist); the Ethnologue-comment also cites Jakway 1975 (hh:hw:Jakway:Palabras). No grammar, sketch or phonology exists in Glottolog.

sources.citation: Jakway, Martha A. (recop.). 1975 [2a ed. 2008]. Listas comparativas de palabras usuales en idiomas vernáculos de la selva. Datos Etno-Lingüísticos 4. Lima: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. Familia Pano section: 'Mayú - recopilada en 1970 por Harriet Fields Hodge en Yaquerana' (printed p. 222) and Mayú column in the Pano tables pp. 226-282.
sources.note: No phonology content. The intro paragraph (p. 222) is ethnographic (informant, ornaments, flight from whites). The handwritten Mayú column has 23 filled cells out of 372; forms carry acute accent marks (e.g. ašk̯óme 'árbol', sáita 'arco' on p. 226) — wordlist-only stress-mark data, no statement or transcription key for accent in the pages read (front matter pp. 3-4 describe collectors/informants only).

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages (ed. Johannes Wilbert). Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center.
sources.note: Nothing. p. 146: 'gg. LANGUAGE OF THE MORIQUE GROUP. Moríque or Mayoruna - spoken on the border of Brazil and Peru, on the Javari River. [Tessmann 1930, pp. 411-414.]' — a classification entry only; it locates the Tessmann wordlist at pp. 411-414.

sources.citation: Tovar, Antonio. 1961. Catálogo de las lenguas de America del Sur: enumeración, con indicaciones tipológicas, bibliografía y mapas. Buenos Aires: Editorial Sudamericana.
sources.note: 'Tenemos que incluir en este grupo al Mayoruna o Morike que nos es conocido por un vocabulario recogido por Tessmann, y que hay que distinguir del homónimo Mayoruna que hemos incluido junto a las lenguas Pano (9.6). Se sitúa sobre el río Javary, y es un dialecto Arawak muy alt[erado]'; classification only, nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Mason, J. Alden. 1950. 'The languages of South American Indians'. In Julian H. Steward (ed.), Handbook of South American Indians, vol. 6 (Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 143), 157-317. Washington: Smithsonian Institution.
sources.note: 'Mayoruna is generally accepted as a Panoan language.. However, Tessmann and Loukotka see nothing Panoan in it. Tessmann (1930) considers it a mixture of Arawak and Tupi; Loukotka gives it independent status, at first (1935) terming it Mayoruna family, Morike language, and later (1939 a) Morike family; he sees Arawak intrusions in it.. It had best be left unclassified; the linguistic data are poor.' No phonology.

sources.citation: Tessmann, Günter. 1930. Die Indianer Nordost-Perus: grundlegende Forschungen für eine systematische Kulturkunde. Hamburg: Friederichsen, de Gruyter. 'Mayoruna' (= Moríke) wordlist pp. 411-414, plus his transcription conventions in the introduction.
sources.note: The only primary attestation of the language. Tessmann marked accent in his transcriptions, so the wordlist entries are the sole possible evidence of Morike word stress; his introduction explains the accent notation. No prose statement about stress is expected.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Morique language' and Wikipedia (pt) 'Língua morique', raw wikitext
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Confirms the only data are Tessmann's 1930 wordlist (from one Moríke man at Requena) and a later Mayú wordlist from Cuibusio (c. 1975, i.e. the SIL/Jakway material); pt page gives an 8-item Moríque–Chamicuro comparison from Ramirez 2019: 658 / 2020 vol. 3: 145 with no stress marks.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2020. Enciclopédia das línguas Arawak: acrescida de seis novas línguas e dois bancos de dados, vol. 3. Curitiba: Editora CRV. Moríke section p. 145 (2019 pre-print p. 658).
